note: The place of the dive (cut/HANDOVER.md S1). oval: the centre of the small orange oval in the wake of the great storm, in degrees on the globe's surface with the flow at rest as frozen for the dive (measured by assets-src/jupiter/plates/place.py on the globe's own imagery). vortex: the centre of the close image's funnel in chart units (measured on the laid back image). The chart of the close view is laid on the globe so that the vortex sits on the oval and the baked Sun of the close image (deck.json light.azimuthDeg) points to the globe's Sun at the handover. freeze: the globe's band flow and the storm's swirl ease to rest from afterDiveStart seconds into the dive over easeSeconds, and the spin stops at the handover, so the place is a rigid ground while it is near. solved is written by the tool: local is the frozen flow time in seconds, toSurface the rotation from the close view's frame to the globe's surface frame (the frame of the lookups, before the spin), n e u the chart's origin and axes there, twinHeight the close camera's height in radii. approach: how the close view comes to the surface view and leaves it. At the first frame of the surface view the camera is the surface view's own camera with its own speed; before it (dive) and after its last frame (rise) the camera is that flight carried on, plus height units up and back units behind along the heading, both times the share of seconds outside the surface view raised to power, so speed and turn rate have no step. Over track seconds the camera takes up a look at the vortex that keeps it where it stands in the frame at that first or last frame. handover: the options of the engine's handover per kind (assets-src/shared/HANDOVER-NOTES.md). freeze.releaseAfterRise: seconds after the handover of the rise from which the frozen flow time is led back to the running one, reached at the end of the rise. exposure.ratio: per channel, the light of the surface view's plates over the globe's light on the same plates at the handover (measured on stills of both sides); the globe is multiplied by it to the power of a share read from the camera's height (scene.grade), the deck's own program by it to the power of the share minus 1, in the dive and in the rise alike, so the exposure is one function of the height with no step at the change of view.

handover.note: The change of view sits at the seams of the surface view (frames 3059 and 3240), so the whole dive and the whole rise are drawn by the globe's group, which holds the deck's own program (scene). No place picture, no sky frames, no limb reach: nothing of the change of view runs on the film's clock. path: the flanks of the engine's glide as shares of the move, until the engine's one move (plan E) is the film's path.

limb.note: The globe's own rim near the place. From orbit the lit edge is drawn a little inside the sphere with a warm glow of air beyond it (look.ts litEdge and edge). Close above the tops that glow is the ground behind the horizon at a low cover, a mottled band tens of pixels wide, and the surface view has no such band. nearHeights: camera height over the sphere in radii; the inset of the lit edge and the cover of the glow are multiplied by a share that runs smoothly in the logarithm of the height from 0 at the first number to 1 at the second, and is exactly 1 above it, so every frame higher than the second number keeps its bytes (the hold, and the judged frames 2997 and 3296).

scene.note: One scene through the change of view (second review note, plan F). Every weight here is read from the height of the camera over the sphere in radii and runs smoothly in the logarithm of the height between its two numbers; nothing is read from the film's clock. ground: the close ground (the deck's plates on the deck's own relief, found by the same march) drawn by the globe's program in place of its own imagery, lit as the globe is lit; all of it at and below the first height, none at and above the second. deck: the deck's own program drawn over the globe; all of it at and below the first height, none of it at and above the second. limb: the same for the deck's own horizon glow, and the globe's shells give way by the same weight. air: the air of the approved view; all of it at and below the first height (which lies above every height of the surface view, so its frames keep their look), none at and above the second, where the ground shows as the globe shows it. grade: the share of the level ratio between the two programs that the globe takes; all at and below the first height, none at and above the second, which lies under the hold's lowest height, so the hold keeps its bytes. It runs evenly in the logarithm of the height, so no frame takes more of the change of level than its share of the fall, with its two ends rounded over gradeRound of the span. sky: the share of the surface view's sky. skyTurn: the turn of the sky and the carry of the stars toward the surface view's.
